evidence.mechanism_source_span: To print high-performance polymers, a stable running printer that can reach high temperatures is needed.

mechanism.mechanism: High-performance polymer printing fails due to the lack of a stable running printer that can reach high temperatures and manipulate process parameters; the mechanism requires an open-source hardware upgrade capable of reaching 500 °C nozzle, 200 °C heated bed, and 135 °C heated chamber with electronics operating within the recommended temperature range to prevent delamination.
mechanism.intervention: Implement the open-source hardware upgrade for low-cost 3D printers using Klipper and Fluidd firmware to continuously monitor and calibrate hardware, ensuring the printer reaches 500 °C nozzle, 200 °C heated bed, and 135 °C heated chamber to stabilize the thermal environment for polycarbonate.
mechanism.expected_effect: The printer produces specimens with excellent surface quality and no signs of delamination, maintaining mechanical integrity by ensuring the stable running printer reaches and maintains the high temperatures necessary for high-performance polymers, thereby preventing layer skipping caused by thermal shock or inconsistent viscosity.
mechanism.falsification_test: If the heated chamber and continuous monitoring are disabled or if the nozzle temperature drops below 500 °C, delamination signs will reappear in the printed polycarbonate specimens, and the measured tensile strength will fall below the 15% outperformance margin in the ZX direction compared to the datasheet.

mechanism.mechanism: Thermal stabilization of high-performance polycarbonate during extrusion via optimized temperature and nozzle velocity to ensure proper material flow and mechanical bonding.
mechanism.intervention: Adjust the print bed temperature to be significantly higher than the 35C ambient threshold (e.g., 80-100C) and calibrate the nozzle velocity to maintain optimal polycarbonate rheology.
mechanism.expected_effect: Reduces thermal shock between the nozzle and the bed, preventing premature solidification of the layer and eliminating the layer skipping phenomenon.
mechanism.falsification_test: Print a tower test with polycarbonate at 35C ambient using bed temperatures of 50C, 80C, and 100C; layer skipping should cease at 80C or higher.

competing_candidates.mechanism: The printability and mechanical integrity of polycarbonate are governed by a coupled thermal-kinetic matrix where nozzle temperature and extrusion velocity determine the rate of crystallization and adhesion between layers, and this sensitivity is exacerbated when the part bed or ambient temperature exceeds specific thresholds, leading to delamination or layer skipping if the cooling profile is insufficient.
competing_candidates.intervention: Implement a closed-loop active cooling system that maintains the build platform and immediate surrounding ambient temperature below 35C, or increase the nozzle temperature and reduce the extrusion velocity (increase dwell time) to compensate for the higher baseline thermal energy, ensuring the thermal budget allows for proper interlayer fusion without premature solidification or delamination.

competing_candidates.mechanism: The use of a two-temperature stage extruder to maintain high polymer viscosity and prevent premature cooling in high-performance polycarbonate
competing_candidates.intervention: Equip the 3D printer with a dual-zone heated nozzle and chamber insulation to ensure the second heating zone maintains polycarbonate above its glass transition temperature during layer deposition

competing_candidates.mechanism: Two-temperature stage extruder maintains elevated melt/feed temperature to keep polycarbonate above its heat-resistant processing window, preventing premature cooling and loss of inter-layer bonding when ambient conditions approach PC's heat-distortion limit.
competing_candidates.intervention: Replace the single-zone hot end with a two-temperature stage extruder for PC, setting the upstream/feed zone to a temperature tuned to keep the melt above the threshold where layer adhesion fails above 35C ambient; monitor and record a single measurement — the inter-layer weld/interface temperature (or equivalently the extrudate surface temperature at deposition) — as the settlement metric.

mechanism.mechanism: Two-temperature stage extruder maintains elevated melt/feed temperature to keep polycarbonate above its heat-resistant processing window, preventing premature cooling and loss of inter-layer bonding when ambient conditions approach PC's heat-distortion limit.
mechanism.intervention: Replace the single-zone hot end with a two-temperature stage extruder for PC, setting the upstream/feed zone to a temperature tuned to keep the melt above the threshold where layer adhesion fails above 35C ambient; monitor and record a single measurement — the inter-layer weld/interface temperature (or equivalently the extrudate surface temperature at deposition) — as the settlement metric.
mechanism.expected_effect: Layer skipping is eliminated (or sharply reduced) above 35C ambient because the two-stage thermal profile keeps the deposited bead hot enough to fuse with the previously laid layer, compensating for the high ambient temperature that would otherwise flash-cool the extrudate against the heat-resistant PC substrate.
mechanism.falsification_test: Print the same PC part with the two-temperature stage extruder at a controlled 38C ambient chamber, sweeping the inter-layer deposition temperature setpoint; the layer-skip failure is falsified only if layer skipping disappears once the measured inter-layer deposition temperature stays above the identified threshold across a statistically adequate number of layers, and reappears when that measurement is forced below threshold on an otherwise identical part.

competing_candidates.mechanism: The printability and mechanical integrity of polycarbonate are governed by a coupled thermal-kinetic matrix where nozzle temperature and extrusion velocity determine the rate of crystallization and adhesion between layers, and this sensitivity is exacerbated when the part bed or ambient temperature exceeds specific thresholds, leading to delamination or layer skipping if the cooling profile is insufficient.
competing_candidates.intervention: Implement a closed-loop active cooling system that maintains the build platform and immediate surrounding ambient temperature below 35C, or increase the nozzle temperature and reduce the extrusion velocity (increase dwell time) to compensate for the higher baseline thermal energy, ensuring the thermal budget allows for proper interlayer fusion without premature solidification or delamination.
